faqs.question: When is Propose Day in 2027?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February. It is the second day of Valentine week, which opens with Rose Day on Sunday 7 February 2027 and closes with Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February 2027.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day before or after Rose Day?
faqs.answer: After. Rose Day is the first day of Valentine week and Propose Day is the second. In 2027 that means Sunday 7 February, then Monday 8 February.

faqs.question: Can I send Propose Day wishes in Marathi to a friend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a lot of people do. Use तुम्ही for a colleague, a senior or a group and तू only for a friend your own age, keep the word प्रेम out of it, and say what the friendship is worth rather than asking for anything — a line like तुमची साथ अशीच राहू द्या reads as warmth, not as a proposal.

faqs.question: Should I use तू or तुम्ही in a Marathi Propose Day message?
faqs.answer: तू for a partner, a close friend or someone your own age you are already informal with. तुम्ही for a spouse in a traditional household, an older person, a colleague or a group. Getting this wrong is the fastest way to make the message land oddly.

faqs.question: How do I know a Marathi line isn't just Hindi written in Devanagari?
faqs.answer: Check the copula and the possessive. Marathi uses आहे, आहेस, आहात and माझा, माझी, माझं; Hindi uses है, हैं and मेरा. Marathi also says तुझ्यावर प्रेम आहे where Hindi says तुमसे प्यार है.

faqs.question: What should I send my wife or husband on Propose Day in Marathi?
faqs.answer: Something that refers to the years already spent, not to a question being asked. In many Marathi households a wife addresses her husband as तुम्ही, so a line such as तुम्ही आहात म्हणून या घराला घरपण आहे fits better than anything phrased as a proposal.

faqs.question: Is it okay to propose again to someone who said no?
faqs.answer: Once, without pressure, and only if the first no was not a firm one. Say plainly that the answer can stay the same — घाई नको, तयार असशील तेव्हा सांग — and then leave it alone.

faqs.question: Should I post the wish as a WhatsApp status or send it privately?
faqs.answer: A status goes to every contact you have at once, which is a public declaration whether you meant it as one or not. If the relationship is not something both families know about, send it in the chat instead.

faqs.question: Do these Marathi lines work if the person reads only Roman script?
faqs.answer: Yes — every line here carries a Roman transliteration, which is what most Marathi speakers type in anyway. Send the transliteration alone, or the Devanagari and the Roman together.

faqs.question: Is a personalised link better than a plain Marathi text message?
faqs.answer: Only when you have something to show, like photographs or a story with a sequence to it. For a single sentence to a friend or a colleague, a plain message in the chat you already use is better, and SubhSandesh is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: Do I have to change the wording if I am a woman sending it?
faqs.answer: Yes, the verb changes with the speaker's gender in Marathi. विचारतो becomes विचारते, सांगतो becomes सांगते, and the endings for the person you address change too — म्हणालीस to a woman, म्हणालास to a man.

faqs.question: Are the SubhSandesh templates available in Marathi?
faqs.answer: No. The template wording, prompts and buttons are all in English; the Marathi is what you type into the page. Your Devanagari is stored and displayed exactly as entered, but a Marathi reader does not get a Marathi interface.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Wishes in Marathi, Sorted by तू or तुम्ही

Propose Day 2027 falls on **Monday 8 February**, the second day of Valentine week — Rose Day is Sunday 7 February, Valentine's Day is Sunday 14 February. The Propose Day wishes in Marathi below are sorted by register — **तू** or **तुम्ही** — and then by how private the screen each one is read on, every line with a Roman transliteration and an English meaning. Who else can see that screen is not a small question: across the 4,567 personalised pages SubhSandesh creators have built since 12 March 2026 — platform-wide, across all 16 page types — 39.9% put a password on the page before sharing it (1,822 of 4,567), and 48.9% of the 51,504 views recorded platform-wide landed on a phone (25,167).

## When is Propose Day 2027, and why the Monday changes things

Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February. Valentine week opens the day before on Rose Day, Sunday 7 February 2027, and closes on Valentine's Day, Sunday 14 February 2027.

In 2026 Propose Day fell on a Sunday, which is why so much circulating advice assumes an open afternoon. A Monday gives you none, and several Marathi pages ranking for this query still carry 2025 or 2026 in their titles.

So the wish goes out before 10am or after 7pm, on a phone, in a chat window — not read aloud across a table.

## What makes a wish Marathi, and not Hindi written in Devanagari

A Marathi wish is not a Hindi wish in the same script. Marathi uses **आहे / आहेस / आहात** where Hindi uses है and हैं, **माझा / माझी / माझं** where Hindi uses मेरा, and **तू / तुम्ही** where Hindi uses तुम and आप — each with its own verb endings.

The clearest tell is the verb for loving. Marathi says **तुझ्यावर प्रेम आहे**, love *on* you; Hindi says तुमसे प्यार है. A line built on the Hindi frame is spotted instantly.

Vocabulary gives it away too: आयुष्य, not ज़िंदगी; धावपळ, not भागदौड़; नशीब, not किस्मत. [Marathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathi_language) has been recorded as a distinct language for centuries: Pär Eliasson's 2025 survey in *Orientalia Suecana* catalogues [Marathi and Konkani dictionary manuscripts](https://journals.uu.se/orientaliasuecana/article/view/654) compiled by European lexicographers in the 1500s and 1600s.

Two variables change nearly every line below: the gender of the person you write to (म्हणालीस to a woman, म्हणालास to a man) and your own (विचारतो if male, विचारते if female). Swap before sending.

## 12 Marathi Propose Day wishes, sorted by register and by screen

Twelve, not a hundred and one. The four **तू** groups come first, most private screen to least; the two **तुम्ही** groups follow.

### 1. तू — a chat only they open: the ask itself


**तुझ्या सोबतीत माझा प्रत्येक दिवस सुंदर होतो. आजपासून कायमची माझी होशील का?**
*Tujhya sobatit majha pratyek divas sundar hoto. Ajpasun kayamchi majhi hoshil ka?*
"Every day turns out beautiful in your company. From today, will you be mine for good?"

**शब्द कमी पडतायत, म्हणून थेट विचारतो — माझ्यासोबत आयुष्य काढायला तयार आहेस का?**
*Shabda kami padtayat, mhanun thet vicharto — majhyasobat ayushya kadhayla tayar ahes ka?*
"Words are falling short, so I'll ask straight: are you ready to spend a life with me?"

### 2. तू — a chat only they open: not said yet


**तुला सांगायचं होतं, पण धीर होत नव्हता. आज सांगून टाकतो — तू मला खूप आवडतेस.**
*Tula sangaycha hota, pan dhir hot navhata. Aj sangun takto — tu mala khup avadtes.*
"I've meant to tell you but couldn't find the nerve. Today I'll just say it: I like you, a lot."

**उत्तर काहीही असो, आपली मैत्री तशीच राहील. एवढं सांगून मग विचारतो.**
*Uttar kahihi aso, apli maitri tashich rahil. Evadha sangun mag vicharto.*
"Whatever the answer, our friendship stays as it is. I'm saying that first, then asking."

### 3. तू — a screen in another city: long distance


**अंतर आहे, पण मनं लांब नाहीत. आज एवढंच विचारतो — वाट बघशील ना?**
*Antar ahe, pan mana lamb nahit. Aj evadhach vicharto — vat baghshil na?*
"There is distance, but our hearts are not far apart. Today I ask only this: will you wait?"

**रोज बोलतो, तरी एक वाक्य राहूनच जातं. आज ते लिहून पाठवतो — तुझ्यावर खूप प्रेम आहे.**
*Roj bolto, tari ek vakya rahunach jata. Aj te lihun pathavto — tujhyavar khup prem ahe.*
"We talk every day, and still one sentence goes unsaid. Today I'm writing it down and sending it: I love you very much."

### 4. तू — a chat you then leave alone: asking again


**मागच्या वेळी नाही म्हणालीस, त्याचा राग नाही. तू आनंदात आहेस, एवढं पुरे.**
*Magchya veli nahi mhanalis, tyacha rag nahi. Tu anandat ahes, evadha pure.*
"You said no last time, and I hold nothing against it. That you are happy is enough."

**घाई नको. तयार असशील तेव्हा सांग — मी इथेच आहे.**
*Ghai nako. Tayar asshil tevha sang — mi ithech ahe.*
"No rush. Tell me when you're ready. I'm right here."

### 5. तुम्ही — a phone the household picks up: husband or wife


**इतकी वर्षं झाली, तरी तुमच्याकडे बघितलं की पहिल्या दिवसासारखं वाटतं. प्रपोज डेच्या शुभेच्छा.**
*Itaki varsha jhali, tari tumchyakade baghitla ki pahilya divsasarkha vatata. Propose Day-chya shubhechchha.*
"So many years gone, and still one look at you feels like the first day. Happy Propose Day."

**रोजच्या धावपळीत सांगायचं राहून जातं — तुम्ही आहात म्हणून या घराला घरपण आहे.**
*Rojchya dhavpalit sangaycha rahun jata — tumhi ahat mhanun ya gharala gharpan ahe.*
"In the daily rush it goes unsaid: this house feels like a home because you are in it."

### 6. तुम्ही or तू — a chat anyone can screenshot: friend or colleague

तू for a friend your own age; तुम्ही for a colleague or a group.


**प्रपोज डे फक्त प्रेमासाठी नाही. तुझ्यासारखा मित्र मिळाला, हेच माझं नशीब.**
*Propose Day fakta premasathi nahi. Tujhyasarkha mitra milala, hech majha nashib.*
"Propose Day is not only for romance. Getting a friend like you is my good fortune."

**आजच्या दिवशी एकच सांगावंसं वाटतं — तुमची साथ अशीच राहू द्या.**
*Ajchya divshi ekach sangavasa vatata — tumchi sath ashich rahu dya.*
"Today I want to say one thing: let your companionship stay exactly as it is."

## Which way of sending it fits which recipient

This compares how a Marathi wish travels, against the privacy you control.

| How you send it | Who it fits | Privacy you control | SubhSandesh platform-wide figure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain text in an existing chat | A friend, colleague or group | None; stays in chat history, forwardable | Not measured — no page created |
| A shareable personalised page | A partner you want to show something | A password, set before you share the link | 39.9% of creators set one (1,822 of 4,567) |
| A handwritten note on paper | Someone in the same room | Complete | Nothing digital exists to measure |

Two of the three rows are unflattering to us; a page earns its place only when there's something to show.

## Sending it quietly, because in Maharashtra that is a real constraint

This is the part wishes pages skip. In a community study of 15–24-year-olds in urban and rural Pune district, [about one-third of urban young people and one-fourth of rural ones reported having made or received a proposal of romantic partnership](https://www.guttmacher.org/journals/ipsrh/2007/12/correlates-premarital-relationships-among-unmarried-youth-pune-district); 24% of urban young men and 8% of urban young women had ever had a romantic partner, against 17% and 5% rurally. 

The authors call Pune a traditional setting where such relationships "are usually carried on secretly", and found strict parental supervision made no difference to whether young people entered one. The paper is from 2007; the proportions are dated, the social shape is not. The same programme published a [Maharashtra brief on romance before marriage](https://knowledgecommons.popcouncil.org/departments_sbsr-pgy/1124/) in 2008.

Family is not the only reader. Parul Bhandari's 2017 New Delhi fieldwork — 100 in-depth interviews with 24–31-year-olds plus about 25 parents — found [partners routinely checking each other's messages, email and whereabouts](https://journals.openedition.org/samaj/4379), with submitting to it read as proof of intimacy rather than control. A Propose Day wish is not sent into an empty room.

The week itself is contested. Hindu nationalist groups mount public actions against Valentine's Day most years; a [14 February 2026 analysis](https://religionunplugged.com/news/2026/2/14/hindu-moral-panic-and-the-policing-of-valentines-day-in-india) records a campus incident in Indore that day. That does not make a Marathi line risky to send; it makes the medium a choice rather than a default.

That is where a lockable page earns its place. The [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) walks your story to a YES button that grows every time the reader dodges it, and locking one does not stop people sending it: platform-wide, 92.7% of started pages get shared. 

If you are not asking anyone to marry you, the [I love you page](/love-gf) is the honest alternative: a declaration rather than a question, and the template the platform's median 6.4-hour first-save-to-last-edit gap was sampled on (n=1,138). For a friend, a colleague or a group, neither is right — send the Marathi line as plain text in the chat you already have, and send no link. You can [check the full template list](/templates) first.

One limit, plainly: every template's wording, prompts and buttons are in English. The page displays the Devanagari you type exactly as entered, but a Marathi reader gets no Marathi interface.

## When a Marathi wish, or a page, is the wrong choice

If the person is in the same room, say the line out loud and send nothing. Speech carries the register a screen flattens.

If they read Roman faster than Devanagari — common among Marathi speakers who type in Roman — send the transliteration instead, or both.

If they do not use a smartphone, a link is the wrong object: 48.9% of the 51,504 views recorded platform-wide were on a phone, which describes the format's assumptions, not a recommendation.

And if nobody in either family knows, be clear what a password does: it stops a casual opener, not your recipient forwarding the link. A handwritten Marathi note leaves no copy anywhere, and SubhSandesh has no data on those at all.

## Sources

- Alexander, M. et al. (2007). "Correlates of Premarital Relationships Among Unmarried Youth in Pune District, Maharashtra, India." *International Family Planning Perspectives* 33(4).
- Bhandari, P. (2017). "Pre-marital Relationships and the Family in Modern India." *South Asia Multidisciplinary Academic Journal* 16.
- IIPS (2008). "Romance and sex before marriage among young women and men in Maharashtra." *Youth in India: Situation and Needs* Policy Brief 5.
- Eliasson, P. (2025). "An Overview of Early Modern Missionary Dictionaries of Konkani and Marathi." *Orientalia Suecana* 74.
- ReligionUnplugged (14 February 2026). "Hindu Moral Panic And The Policing Of Valentine's Day In India."

failed.why: The Orientalia Suecana lexicography survey would sit unchanged in any Marathi-language keyword in this batch; the other four sources are Maharashtra-, surveillance- or Valentine-specific and would not transfer. Replacing it needs a source narrow enough to be about Marathi second-person register rather than Marathi as a language, and this fix pass had no working fetch path — WebFetch is denied on this machine and the session's 200 WebSearch calls are spent — so no candidate could be fetched, read or verified, and citing one from memory is not permitted. It is kept rather than dropped because the Marathi-is-not-Hindi section needs a citable statement that Marathi is a separately documented language. Closes when a fetch path is restored and a descriptive grammar or a sociolinguistic study of Marathi honorific address (तू / तुम्ही) is found open-access and read in full; re-check at the start of the next batch.

auditReport.honestAssessment: This is the only Marathi Propose Day page organised by grammatical register rather than by recipient: every line is labelled तू or तुम्ही and then placed by how private the screen it will be read on is, with a Roman transliteration and an English gloss on each, the verified 2027 weekday printed, and the discretion problem grounded in Pune-district research instead of assertion — none of which the Loksatta, Maharashtra Times, Webdunia, Lokmat or MensXP pages do. The re-cut removes the earlier convergence with MensXP's recipient segmentation, but two of the six incumbents (Zee, Times Now) returned 403 to a direct fetch and were never structurally analysed, so the no-mirroring claim is verified against four of six pages, not all six.
